1.explanation: Prism’s JSON definition currently extends the JavaScript grammar, which brings in C-style comment tokens (the /* … */ pattern). Because the JSON ‘string’ token is not marked greedy or ordered to run before the comment tokens, the sequence “/*” in a JSON string triggers the JavaScript comment rule. The fix must remove or override the comment patterns from the JSON grammar (in components/prism-json.js and its minified counterpart) and then rebuild prism.js so the core bundle no longer mis-tokenizes “/*” inside JSON strings.
1.bug_scenario: When Prism highlights JSON (with the language-json class) any occurrence of “/*” inside a JSON string is being interpreted as the start of a C-style comment. In the screenshot you can see a JSON object where the first property’s value is the two-character string “/*”. Instead of treating it as part of a string, Prism’s tokenizer drops into a comment mode and leaves the rest of the JSON un-highlighted.

2.explanation: The bug stems from the JSON syntax definition in prism-json.js (and its minified counterpart). In that file, Prism inherits the JavaScript comment patterns and does not prevent the comment‐start sequence “/*” from matching inside JSON string literals. As a result, the tokenizer treats “/*” inside a string as the beginning of a comment. To fix the issue, the JSON definition (prism-json.js) must be changed to disable or override the comment pattern so that “/*” inside quoted strings is not recognized as a comment delimiter.
2.bug_scenario: When Prism is used to highlight JSON, a JSON string value that contains the characters “/*” (for example, {"A": "/*", "B": "B", "C": "C"}) is tokenized as the start of a comment. Everything after that point is treated as comment text, causing the closing quote and the rest of the JSON to be mis-highlighted. This happens with an HTTP response whose Accept header is “*/*” (so the JSON is highlighted with the JSON grammar) and still occurs in the latest version of Prism.
